name: Maurice Mitchell, WFP
subject: We are witnessing a hostile takeover
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Working Families Party PAC (77 Sands St
body:
| | | Peter, We’re now a little over three weeks into the second Trump administration, and if you’re like me, it feels like their attacks have been non-stop. I want to take a few minutes to recap some of the most dangerous proposals and tactics I’m seeing from Trump and Musk so far. And also to share some thoughts about what I feel should be our core vision and focus at this moment. **First, the recap.** Over the last few weeks we have been witnessing a hostile takeover of government at virtually every level. Billionaires are now running the federal government, and they are trying to loot, plunder, and pillage as much and as quickly as they can, no matter how many working families get hurt:
* The hijacking of the Treasury Department and other key agencies in an effort to gut federal funding for things like Medicaid, school lunches, family farm subsidies, veterans benefits, and cancer research.
* The attempted dismantling of the Department of Education.
* Opening the gates for rampant corruption by firing the head of the Office of Government Ethics, firing nearly every U.S. Inspector General, and halting the enforcement of anti-bribery acts.
* High-profile deportations and ICE raids nationwide.
* The theft of our personal information, with Musk’s staff gaining access to the social security numbers, taxpayer info, and other personal data of every single person in the country.
* Deleting thousands of webpages that previously provided crucial public health resources and FAQs.

It’s a blitzkrieg. And it is understandable to feel disoriented or afraid. **But know that we are not powerless — not by a longshot.** Not only have we ALREADY forced Trump and Musk to back down from some of their plans, but our opposition can grow even fiercer from here, as long as we stay grounded, focused, and vigilant. **It’s been said before — but this truly is going to be a marathon, not a sprint.** I know how overwhelming it feels to see attack after attack every day. But we need to remember that when we come together, we have the power. And that retreating to cynicism, or taking the bait when negative messages come raining down, won’t help. This is why I have not joined the “FAFO” crowd. I do not scold or belittle working people, including Trump voters. At the end of the day, no working-class person is my enemy, even the ones I disagree with, especially at a time when the billionaire class seeks to do so much harm to so many, including those they conned to root them on. So we need to respond to the attacks from Trump, the GOP, and the billionaires they’ve literally walked into the White House by shedding a light on their true motive: **trying to turn us against one another while they laugh all the way to the bank.** **At the same time, let’s also affirm that the status quo before this was not working for our families either.** That’s why we are ultimately working to end a two-party system that has never worked for any of us. We know it’s possible, because we’ve already broken through in some cities and states. We believe that working people should govern. We know billionaires like Elon Musk did not “earn” their wealth, that they inherited some and stole the rest. So if we want to address climate change or make the economy work for everyone, or take on any big challenge, that means WE need to take the wheel. **And to GAIN that power, we need to widen our tent.** Our nation is going to be facing a series of crises. At each of them, there will be opportunities for us to recruit more people to this movement. And that’s where our focus needs to be. If a Trump voter says “I didn’t vote for this,” that’s our chance to welcome them into an irresistible, compassionate, and strategic solidarity movement that has a lot more to offer them than the “broligarchy.” And if you know people who stayed home on election day last year, don’t throw the blame at their feet either — find out the source of their disillusionment, and invite them to join us in building something better. Remember, it’s never too late to join the fight. That’s how I am viewing this moment and our path ahead right now. But I’d love to hear your thoughts, reactions, and feedback too. clean_body: | | | Peter, We’re now a little over three weeks into the second Trump administration, and if you’re like me, it feels like their attacks have been non-stop. I want to take a few minutes to recap some of the most dangerous proposals and tactics I’m seeing from Trump and Musk so far. And also to share some thoughts about what I feel should be our core vision and focus at this moment. First, the recap. Over the last few weeks we have been witnessing a hostile takeover of government at virtually every level. Billionaires are now running the federal government, and they are trying to loot, plunder, and pillage as much and as quickly as they can, no matter how many working families get hurt: The hijacking of the Treasury Department and other key agencies in an effort to gut federal funding for things like Medicaid, school lunches, family farm subsidies, veterans benefits, and cancer research. The attempted dismantling of the Department of Education. Opening the gates for rampant corruption by firing the head of the Office of Government Ethics, firing nearly every U.S. Inspector General, and halting the enforcement of anti-bribery acts. High-profile deportations and ICE raids nationwide. The theft of our personal information, with Musk’s staff gaining access to the social security numbers, taxpayer info, and other personal data of every single person in the country. Deleting thousands of webpages that previously provided crucial public health resources and FAQs. It’s a blitzkrieg. And it is understandable to feel disoriented or afraid. But know that we are not powerless — not by a longshot. Not only have we ALREADY forced Trump and Musk to back down from some of their plans, but our opposition can grow even fiercer from here, as long as we stay grounded, focused, and vigilant. It’s been said before — but this truly is going to be a marathon, not a sprint. I know how overwhelming it feels to see attack after attack every day. But we need to remember that when we come together, we have the power. And that retreating to cynicism, or taking the bait when negative messages come raining down, won’t help. This is why I have not joined the “FAFO” crowd. I do not scold or belittle working people, including Trump voters. At the end of the day, no working-class person is my enemy, even the ones I disagree with, especially at a time when the billionaire class seeks to do so much harm to so many, including those they conned to root them on. So we need to respond to the attacks from Trump, the GOP, and the billionaires they’ve literally walked into the White House by shedding a light on their true motive: trying to turn us against one another while they laugh all the way to the bank. At the same time, let’s also affirm that the status quo before this was not working for our families either. That’s why we are ultimately working to end a two-party system that has never worked for any of us. We know it’s possible, because we’ve already broken through in some cities and states. We believe that working people should govern. We know billionaires like Elon Musk did not “earn” their wealth, that they inherited some and stole the rest. So if we want to address climate change or make the economy work for everyone, or take on any big challenge, that means WE need to take the wheel. And to GAIN that power, we need to widen our tent. Our nation is going to be facing a series of crises. At each of them, there will be opportunities for us to recruit more people to this movement. And that’s where our focus needs to be. If a Trump voter says “I didn’t vote for this,” that’s our chance to welcome them into an irresistible, compassionate, and strategic solidarity movement that has a lot more to offer them than the “broligarchy.” And if you know people who stayed home on election day last year, don’t throw the blame at their feet either — find out the source of their disillusionment, and invite them to join us in building something better. Remember, it’s never too late to join the fight. That’s how I am viewing this moment and our path ahead right now. But I’d love to hear your thoughts, reactions, and feedback too. With love and solidarity, Maurice Mitchell National Director Working Families Party We are NOT powerless against Trump and Musk and the billionaires — not by a longshot. But in order for our movement to grow stronger, broader, and more durable, we need to keep up our organizing day-in and day-out. Thoughts? Feedback? We want to hear it. # **Karoline Leavitt SLAMS CNN's Kaitlan Collins for challenging Trump 's "Gulf of America" rebrand**
White House Press Secretary **[Karoline Leavitt laid down the law](https://substack.com/redirect/9577036f-80cc-4d6e-82da-27dca51f59e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on Wednesday when CNN reporter Kaitlan Collins challenged Trump's decision to bar Associated Press (AP) reporters from the press pool for not using the new "Gulf of America" nomenclature.
[Watch Video](https://substack.com/redirect/9577036f-80cc-4d6e-82da-27dca51f59e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[](https://substack.com/redirect/9577036f-80cc-4d6e-82da-27dca51f59e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Leavitt assured Collins that the new administration would crack down on fake news being reported by press pool members.
"It is a PRIVILEGE to cover this White House! ... Nobody has the right to go into the Oval Office and ask the President of the United States questions. That's an invitation that is given," Leavitt said.
The exclusion stemmed from**[the AP's refusal to properly identify the Gulf of America ](https://substack.com/redirect/221692c8-a626-4e91-8e97-684fc446fcb4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**in conjunction with President Donald Trump's executive order signed on January 20.
Collins protested that the exclusion violated free speech values that Trump claimed to support.
"If we feel that there are lies being pushed by outlets in this room, we are going to hold those lies accountable," Leavitt fired back. "It is a fact that the body of water off the coast of Louisiana is called the Gulf of America, and I'm not sure why news outlets don't want to call it that, but that is what it is!"
Watch the clash right here:

Dear Friend, Your State Freedom Caucuses continue to do amazing work on your behalf. Before we get to the highlights below, please check out [my latest op-ed](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjo14OgpGP35sI5vBCzgz-2Fk4p3iXh9vV-2Fx2RBdR7OzL0Y15eJ-2FFUMD-2Brd75z79A-2Frjj-2Fx4CmL-2Bwn5tSaBbOzFsWNkf-2BbdNgbi2Ytj-2F6k2UAEtRwKFxyteD2mPSvwLdORft1k468EUmR-2BWYIK2lrsMPlc-3DPIMc_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHerxXGbDCo-2BZ-2F-2FSU0FCzNVPLC5HzBCjUU-2Be5BruXzaEIQq1kmfVxxGolp-2FXO0-2BNohGtQbM0zMc8OjdAJTHUg2B-2FOEXKUFbUlaaRQS-2BMgwb2xS5eorzkKW3vOajg8czqbeqXJgdqTlg6caswVpXXKOxJ-2BLzUhXxVPRQDN41KMm7li9IVO2L1YoRXBYa-2Fr3hCwrUP2VL9t03877zHgQn78Y7pM0jo2La7oJWudfxuhfuEdoAlHUEjEl5-2FuBzXTrbrTmW7) in The Federalist. While we don't have a freedom caucus in Texas and Florida (yet), we've been tracking the shenanigans that have been going on in those two states with Democrats and liberal Republicans conspiring to defeat conservative reforms. Key excerpt: _"Washington, D.C., isn’t the only swamp that needs draining. There are 50 swamps in the 50 state capitols, and they are spiraling out of control. Recent events have made this clear, and their actions should alarm all of us."_**ARIZONA** The **Arizona Freedom Caucus** is on a roll. They've been sponsoring and passing great legislation. Here are a few examples: All AZFC members co-sponsored [HB 2703](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjkMu-2FhzWFDGSBq8utfGCvsw-2FISoznOCypg2-2BLoJK3u2Ssw-2Bws7HXrEADCQWH9fDsL-2BRizhi0S9BYSoHNGV1HF2I-3DFMLa_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHerxXGbDCo-2BZ-2F-2FSU0FCzNVPLC5HzBCjUU-2Be5BruXzaEIQq1kmfVxxGolp-2FXO0-2BNohGtQbM0zMc8OjdAJTHUg2B-2FOOQFWI0z9X1ye679ZQAcRA-2FhKDoPlX7UTtOiQ4DqTrWGlwXBIoCeF9V9vepTjvdm9go48cQtNzFSb8xJ9bbff4h1koUBylweuxT9E844xNp-2BJ6UIJ33kfX3i97Zb5dahVKaP9-2BT-2Bu8m1Vm-2FUSVXGiuh1Fev-2B94RXEkVps5-2Bpzx4u), which passed the House and Senate this week. It would make Arizona elections more like Florida elections - more secure procedures with results actually released on election night! The bill will now head to the Democrat Governor's desk. The AZFC has demanded that she sign it or she will own the mess that the state is currently in. Meanwhile, the AZ House just passed another AZFC-sponsored bill - [HB 2081](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjl5XCzTgrEw27C3pLWfYLwSjWBRKYMGg7Nn6yYtbQJzDUaXtVInaYQsZTXNiRaLrRkdh5Uz-2Bl8BY07ulyOEKR-2BajtwzOZquRWuwYq4CWnvy8jYE__9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHerxXGbDCo-2BZ-2F-2FSU0FCzNVPLC5HzBCjUU-2Be5BruXzaEIQq1kmfVxxGolp-2FXO0-2BNohGtQbM0zMc8OjdAJTHUg2B-2FOLltKSQQ3vM6U5kRKAtUo38GnWByRTvViVDBWPhytAhYr1uELg3jFKRgitic0kP4V3cHup74Hw0BndCXAQwmlb10IxntvW5dFtZmAs31lshPHcPB816u9s9-2BT8k-2BvpoVbZQ0tko0cFy22sr0C6wXyrsyQgMTHlsDKwGJDxbPvHIG) \- which would implement President Trump's "No Tax on Tips" at the state level. The AZ House also passed [HCR 2002](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjhSJ1H1-2FnpS9sZHPaYkM8cfOCFLkBRU4Rt0a8vLQcDvLGW2PzIdd8aLcm3yZWP6K2Q-3D-3DTAmD_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHerxXGbDCo-2BZ-2F-2FSU0FCzNVPLC5HzBCjUU-2Be5BruXzaEIQq1kmfVxxGolp-2FXO0-2BNohGtQbM0zMc8OjdAJTHUg2B-2FOFWq8qDAHQy2bpWIzuh6NKVwBIf85ojtv7H37uBQJK6mcznLrQcrz7p9F4JC4yMuPWkq2-2BCSRxaETB54tk8Do6SXGtrchGQA0-2FUPENHaZXMSijL6hqPKvwdI101fiXJgRRsGOSmBKJZ0qRC8iz5uCDV4ytrfrAjZiwkhaZtb7rbD), which would get rid of "vote centers", and return to precinct voting. Democrats love vote centers because it's confusing to voters and offers more opportunities for fraud. This bill would bypass the governor and go straight to the ballot for approval by the voters.Finally, AZFC Chairman Jake Hoffman got the Democrats to say the quiet part out loud in a committee hearing. They want non-citizens to be counted as part of the U.S. Census. [Watch the viral video here.](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjmPbPfpIZwFstTynsz30VZRkCI8SZL2o2VBonDwWaCfcXvvMhY7rsp5esOcN98Y7yA-3D-3DNA_1_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHerxXGbDCo-2BZ-2F-2FSU0FCzNVPLC5HzBCjUU-2Be5BruXzaEIQq1kmfVxxGolp-2FXO0-2BNohGtQbM0zMc8OjdAJTHUg2B-2FOOUbXWoNFbSdzgUMvsbE-2BLNDx78bUDHO7M-2FWbBZ4Lx4zC8lxRFhPaT7-2FTyYnfuNPRcdPd-2FcAulWKhl-2BDAZfTxK3vfzkpowJ-2Bdx2Mn09oo7q-2BtJg5-2BSsDrgt1ENpn-2F8IpPKcOHdHZC5Ft-2FijJ9XicJv3L19D5bOCGO3rUnpWVv-2Fvy)**WYOMING** The **Wyoming Freedom Caucus** successfully pushed all of their top priorities through the WY House. criticize the ruling – and it’s not even clear if they plan to comply (or
how we’ll know for sure if they did!).

succeeds in slashing SSA funding, which gets payments out to 70 million

name: Tim Kaine
subject: A multi-level strategy to stop Trump’s lawless behavior and save our democracy
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Kaine for Virginia
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-cgp-2025 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-cgp-2025]
Derek:
It’s a difficult time. People are confused and frightened by the onslaught of punishing actions by President Trump and his cronies.
And I hear, loud and clear, many say: “Please do more!”
I want to share the multi-level strategy we are pursuing to stop Donald Trump’s lawless behavior and save our democracy:
It has 5 parts: Courts, Congress, States, Elections, and Activism.
______________
Courts
First, Democrats are part of a well-coordinated Court strategy to stop lawlessness. We implemented this on Inauguration Day and have had great success so far in lawsuits to protect federal workers — a judge has already paused the sham federal worker buyout — stop erosion of constitutional rights, preserve congressional power of the purse, protect immigrants, and restrict people like Elon Musk from rampaging through federal agencies. We won’t win all these cases, but initial signs are positive.
Congress
In Congress, Democrats are in a minority. But we forced the withdrawal of an Attorney General nominee, and I led an effort that gained three Republican votes against the Secretary of Defense. In the coming weeks, we are prepared to wage major battles on the budget and GOP plans to give tax breaks to the wealthy — and I’ve recently used an unusual Senate procedure to set up a challenge to Trump’s plans to gut environmental protections and clean energy projects to benefit Big Oil.
States
Democratic Governors and other officials are acting at the state and local levels to alert the public to the damage caused by Trump budget cuts — and are doing everything possible to protect our neighbors from lawless acts.
Elections
We began 2025 winning key special elections in Virginia and Iowa, and the momentum is growing! I am particularly focused on the Virginia Governor’s race this year, which can send a national message of revulsion over Trump’s failures, so I hope you will join me in getting involved. Virginia will also hold elections for our Lieutenant Governor and Attorney General, both of which we can flip to Democratic leaders, and our House of Delegates, where we must maintain our majority. Your efforts in Virginia’s 2025 elections will be crucial to Democratic success — and the message it will send.
We also need to gear up for a strong showing in the 2026 midterm elections — yes, already. In about 20 months, we have the opportunity to disrupt the GOP trifecta, re-elect strong leaders like my friend Mark Warner [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-cgp-2025-warner] , and establish an opposition better able to fight back against this extreme Administration.
Activism
And finally — your activism matters . Vigorous, peaceful public protest is building all across this nation. Our Founders knew that elections were not sufficient to safeguard democracy, so they protected the right of the people “peacefully to assemble and petition the government for a redress of grievances.” Your dedication is an integral part of our path forward.
This year, we will need you to be involved. In speaking up, in calling out dangerous actions, and in holding accountable those who refuse to use their power to protect democracy. Many of you have visited my Senate offices to discuss issues you care about, and I love seeing you — thank you for being so active. I also need your help expanding our reach in challenging areas, because your voice is powerful. There are many members of Congress in redder areas who desperately need to hear from an impassioned public, and I encourage you to organize in their offices with the same enthusiasm I see in mine.
I’m counting on your resolve, because I’ve seen what we can accomplish with you in the fight.
______________
It’s hard now. But I’m up for the battle ahead, and I feel energized by your active support. The nation is counting on us as we near the 250th birthday of our democracy.
We will prevail!
-TK
Tim Kaine

# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/9?t=1&akid=39435%2E3422442%2EJAZQ9I)
Derek,
I joined CNN on Tuesday to talk about Trump’s attacks on the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB).
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ttp-em-20250213?refcode=em20250213-39435&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&refcode2=39435_3422442_JAZQ9I&akid=39435%2E3422442%2EJAZQ9I)
It’s total BS for Trump to say that he's getting rid of the CFPB because they engage in fraud, when **their entire mission is to fight fraud.**
The CFPB was created in 2011 after the mortgage foreclosure crisis to _protect consumers_. It’s designed to make sure the financial markets–things like car and student loans–don’t take advantage of consumers.
Our whole economy will suffer with the shutdown of the CFPB. Not just consumers, but every business who plays by the rules. _Everyone_ benefits when markets stay strong and consumers aren’t getting cheated.
**[You can check out the rest of the interview here. I also hope you donate to my PAC, Truth to Power, so we can continue to elect candidates who will stand up for consumers.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ttp-em-20250213?refcode=em20250213-39435&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&refcode2=39435_3422442_JAZQ9I&akid=39435%2E3422442%2EJAZQ9I)**

Thank you,
Katie Porter

Unelected, unaccountable and out of control billionaires are buying power and influence in Trump’s Washington, Peter.

**What kind of America are we trying to create?**

Housing costs are too high.
Grocery costs are too high.
Insurance costs are too high.
Childcare costs are too high.
Utility costs are too high.
**America is too expensive, Peter.**

It is **not** acceptable -- in the wealthiest country in the history of the world -- for countless families to be forced to live paycheck to paycheck.

As Trump's Billionaire-First agenda takes shape and his wealthy benefactors claim exclusive access to our democracy, Democrats are the only ones committed to lowering costs for hardworking taxpayers.

Peter, it’s George. Over the past three weeks, we’ve watched Donald Trump and Elon Musk unleash a wave of chaos over Washington — and from what we’ve heard, this is just the beginning. Peter, we have a saying where I come from: **_"Don't watch the mouth, watch the hands."_** We must stay vigilant about this Administration's motives no matter how outrageous their statements. In times like this, we have to remember that _chaos is the point._ Donald Trump and Elon Musk think that by unleashing a barrage of rapid attacks on our institutions and progress, we’ll be paralyzed with shock and leave them unchallenged in their blatant power grabs. Well, I’ve got news for them: I’m not the type to back down from a tough fight — especially when the lives of everyday Americans are on the line. I'm continuing to work with leaders at all levels to push back on this Administration and its unlawful actions, but Peter, I need to know that you’re with me. [Before my February mid-month fundraising deadline in just a few short days, I need to raise $5,000 to prove our strength and take on Trump in Washington. Team, did the American people elected Donald Trump or Elon M usk, as the president in November?
Recently, it’s been tough to figure out who is really making the decisions in the White House.
Here’s what Elon Musk and his Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) has tried to do in the last three weeks:
* Gut USAID, which provides critical resources to prevent disease and famine abroad and at home.

* Slash funding for the National Institute of Health (NIH) which funds vital research into cancer and disease.

* Dismantle the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB), which was created after the 2008 Wall Street crash to protect American consumers, like you, from predatory financial institutions.

* Gain control of the Treasury Department's payment system, putting the private information of millions of Americans at risk.

* Undermine National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), which leads the world in climate science.
Elon's not stopping there. DOGE has also been drawing up plans to carve up the Department of Defense, the Department of Veterans Affairs, and the Department of Education.
Elon Musk, whose net worth is nearly $400 billion, used his immense wealth and influence to help elect Donald Trump and gain access to the White House. Now, he has free rein from Trump to do whatever he wants.

If you’re passionate about real political talk and uncovering hidden truths, [this is the episode you can’t afford to miss!](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=6ec5fab531&e=567664f14c)

# What You’ll Hear in This Episode:
---
| → **Den Haaland’s Gubernatorial Bid:**
Former Congresswoman and Interior Secretary Den Haaland is running for Governor of New Mexico. Mark explains how Haaland’s campaign strategy is likely to unfold and why she must keep her carefully crafted image under wraps to avoid exposing her vulnerabilities. He also dives deep into two disqualifying policies she supports that could cost her the race.
→ **Albuquerque City Attorney’s Controversial Memo:**
Krysty breaks down a new memo urging city employees to record ICE officers and contact city lawyers to slow down criminal deportations. How can a city choose to side with criminals over its own people? We discuss the implications and the growing frustration among citizens.
---
| [Stream Episode Now](https://nodoubtaboutitpodcast.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=d2649c77b4f4f1f9d512804d2&id=7de818db8a&e=567664f14c)
---
| → **The Worst Protest Song Ever:**
You won’t believe your ears! We reveal a hideous anti-DOGE protest song that’s so bad, it will make your ears bleed. You really have to hear it to believe it. Unfortunately, once you do hear it you will never be the same.
→ **Trump Administration & Government Spending Accountability: **
We take a hard look at the ongoing battle pitting the Trump administration against the deep state over cutting waste, fraud, and abuse. Who is fighting to keep the government grift alive, and what does this mean for our future?
→ **CBS Poll Shows Trump’s Surging Support:**
A new CBS news poll reveals that Trump is gaining strong numbers, especially with a key voting block that will surprise you. Mark warns that while Trump may be riding high, he still faces a critical issue that could bring his good times crashing down—find out what it is!
---

# The Value of Party Registration
### Closed Primaries
| | | [Dan Carr](https://substack.com/@freedomfrontline1776)
---
| Feb 13
---
| [](https://substack.com/@freedomfrontline1776)
---
Voting is one of the most important rights we have as Americans. It is how we choose those who represent us and influence the direction of our country. But the way we run elections matters just as much as the act of voting itself. I believe three key things could make our system work better: requiring party registration, holding closed primaries, and moving elections to Saturdays.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/91581a22-80c2-40d5-ad5f-1f25f8926757?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
These changes could bring more fairness, clarity, and participation to the process while also ensuring election security and integrity. One thing we must remember as Americans is that people gave their lives for the right of us being able to vote. So voting should be simple, safe, and secure!! "**Texas could sell 100 miles of border to feds, DPS has same powers as ICE, Abbott says,** " Texas Tribune's**Matthew Choi** -- "More than 100 miles of Texas' borderlands could be leased or sold to the federal government as part of the state's partnership with President **Donald Trump** to harden the border, Gov. **Greg Abbott** said in an interview with The Texas Tribune on Thursday.

Abbott is in Washington this week to lobby Congress for $11 billion to compensate Texas for money spent on his Operation Lone Star initiative, which he said was needed to fill gaps in the Biden administration's immigration enforcement. The three-term Texas governor said he was ready to hand over to the federal government more than 50 miles of constructed border wall, nearly 20 miles of planned border walls, 100 miles of easements to build more walls, over 2,000 military beds for National Guardsmen and 4,000 jail cells to detain migrants.

The exchange of real estate and working border infrastructure built under Operation Lone Star differentiates this request from past appeals Texas has made to the federal government for border enforcement, Abbott said.

"This is not really a reimbursement," said Abbott during a 10-minute interview at his Washington hotel. "This is a payment for real estate assets and improvements provided by the state of Texas as payment for services rendered by the state of Texas that benefits everybody in the United States of America."
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $7/mo](https://substack.com/redirect/6d903fdc-89ae-4902-be33-4840cd20e402?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Texas contains more of the southern border than any other state, stretching over 1,200 miles. Texas officials have long boasted having very little federally controlled land relative to its size.

Abbott met with Texas Republicans and House Speaker **Mike Johnson** this week to make his case, as well as White House officials. Abbott also met with Trump last week.

It remains to be seen if Congress will allocate the funds or if Trump will support the move. Slashing federal spending is among Republicans' highest priorities this year. Abbott didn't say if his meetings with Johnson or Trump yielded support, but he described them as "very appreciative of everything that Texas did, and they thank us for Texas holding the line during the four years of open border policies under [President] **Joe Biden**."
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $70/yr](https://substack.com/redirect/6d903fdc-89ae-4902-be33-4840cd20e402?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Texas Republicans expressed unity and optimism about getting the reimbursement passed. Sen. **John Cornyn** has been one of the leading voices in the effort in Congress and said the Texas delegation can use its large numbers to push the priority to the forefront of Congress' attention. Texas sends more Republicans than any other state.

Cornyn added Abbott's request is "a unique situation" because the money is for "expenses that were incurred by the state that should not have been incurred by the state, but for the failure of the federal government."

House Budget Chair **Jodey Arrington** , R-Lubbock, presented a draft budget resolution Wednesday, which would include $300 billion for border security and defense spending. Arrington supports the payment to Texas, calling it "the right and responsible thing" to do. But he acknowledged he would need to make sure whatever mechanism to send out the money is fiscally responsible. That would mean collaborating with members outside of the Texas delegation.

U.S. Rep. **Chip Roy** , one of the most hawkish conservatives on reining in spending, was supportive of the reimbursement, saying Texas invested in infrastructure the federal government should have built.

"$11 billion came out of the pockets of Texans. That's money that could be used for roads, for schools, for DPS, who should have been in Austin and Dallas and Dallas and San Antonio and Houston and not down on the border," Roy said. "They were doing the job the federal government was supposed to do."

U.S. Rep. **John Carter** , R-Round Rock, serves on the House Appropriations Committee and said he was confident all Republicans on the committee would support the effort. He said it would be an easier sell because the infrastructure is already in place." TOP NEWS "Texas could sell 100 miles of border to feds, DPS has same powers as ICE, Abbott says, " Texas Tribune'sMatthew Choi -- "More than 100 miles of Texas' borderlands could be leased or sold to the federal government as part of the state's partnership with President Donald Trump to harden the border, Gov. Greg Abbott said in an interview with The Texas Tribune on Thursday. Abbott is in Washington this week to lobby Congress for $11 billion to compensate Texas for money spent on his Operation Lone Star initiative, which he said was needed to fill gaps in the Biden administration's immigration enforcement. The three-term Texas governor said he was ready to hand over to the federal government more than 50 miles of constructed border wall, nearly 20 miles of planned border walls, 100 miles of easements to build more walls, over 2,000 military beds for National Guardsmen and 4,000 jail cells to detain migrants. The exchange of real estate and working border infrastructure built under Operation Lone Star differentiates this request from past appeals Texas has made to the federal government for border enforcement, Abbott said. "This is not really a reimbursement," said Abbott during a 10-minute interview at his Washington hotel. "This is a payment for real estate assets and improvements provided by the state of Texas as payment for services rendered by the state of Texas that benefits everybody in the United States of America." Texas contains more of the southern border than any other state, stretching over 1,200 miles. Texas officials have long boasted having very little federally controlled land relative to its size. Abbott met with Texas Republicans and House Speaker Mike Johnson this week to make his case, as well as White House officials. Abbott also met with Trump last week. It remains to be seen if Congress will allocate the funds or if Trump will support the move. Slashing federal spending is among Republicans' highest priorities this year. Abbott didn't say if his meetings with Johnson or Trump yielded support, but he described them as "very appreciative of everything that Texas did, and they thank us for Texas holding the line during the four years of open border policies under [President] Joe Biden." Texas Republicans expressed unity and optimism about getting the reimbursement passed. Sen. John Cornyn has been one of the leading voices in the effort in Congress and said the Texas delegation can use its large numbers to push the priority to the forefront of Congress' attention. Texas sends more Republicans than any other state. Cornyn added Abbott's request is "a unique situation" because the money is for "expenses that were incurred by the state that should not have been incurred by the state, but for the failure of the federal government." House Budget Chair Jodey Arrington , R-Lubbock, presented a draft budget resolution Wednesday, which would include $300 billion for border security and defense spending. Arrington supports the payment to Texas, calling it "the right and responsible thing" to do. But he acknowledged he would need to make sure whatever mechanism to send out the money is fiscally responsible. That would mean collaborating with members outside of the Texas delegation. U.S. Rep. Chip Roy , one of the most hawkish conservatives on reining in spending, was supportive of the reimbursement, saying Texas invested in infrastructure the federal government should have built. "$11 billion came out of the pockets of Texans. That's money that could be used for roads, for schools, for DPS, who should have been in Austin and Dallas and Dallas and San Antonio and Houston and not down on the border," Roy said. "They were doing the job the federal government was supposed to do." U.S. Rep. John Carter , R-Round Rock, serves on the House Appropriations Committee and said he was confident all Republicans on the committee would support the effort. He said it would be an easier sell because the infrastructure is already in place." FREE SUBSCRIPTIONS HAVE ENDED : As of July 11, 2022, we have moved to a paywall for free subscribers. * **TOP NEWS**

"**Texas could sell 100 miles of border to feds, DPS has same powers as ICE, Abbott says,** " Texas Tribune's**Matthew Choi** -- "More than 100 miles of Texas' borderlands could be leased or sold to the federal government as part of the state's partnership with President **Donald Trump** to harden the border, Gov. **Greg Abbott** said in an interview with The Texas Tribune on Thursday.

Abbott is in Washington this week to lobby Congress for $11 billion to compensate Texas for money spent on his Operation Lone Star initiative, which he said was needed to fill gaps in the Biden administration's immigration enforcement. The three-term Texas governor said he was ready to hand over to the federal government more than 50 miles of constructed border wall, nearly 20 miles of planned border walls, 100 miles of easements to build more walls, over 2,000 military beds for National Guardsmen and 4,000 jail cells to detain migrants.

The exchange of real estate and working border infrastructure built under Operation Lone Star differentiates this request from past appeals Texas has made to the federal government for border enforcement, Abbott said.

"This is not really a reimbursement," said Abbott during a 10-minute interview at his Washington hotel. "This is a payment for real estate assets and improvements provided by the state of Texas as payment for services rendered by the state of Texas that benefits everybody in the United States of America."
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $7/mo](https://substack.com/redirect/4bdc1f4d-37f3-4187-8d01-a79380366776?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Texas contains more of the southern border than any other state, stretching over 1,200 miles. Texas officials have long boasted having very little federally controlled land relative to its size.

Abbott met with Texas Republicans and House Speaker **Mike Johnson** this week to make his case, as well as White House officials. Abbott also met with Trump last week.

It remains to be seen if Congress will allocate the funds or if Trump will support the move. Slashing federal spending is among Republicans' highest priorities this year. Abbott didn't say if his meetings with Johnson or Trump yielded support, but he described them as "very appreciative of everything that Texas did, and they thank us for Texas holding the line during the four years of open border policies under [President] **Joe Biden**."

Texas Republicans expressed unity and optimism about getting the reimbursement passed. Sen. **John Cornyn** has been one of the leading voices in the effort in Congress and said the Texas delegation can use its large numbers to push the priority to the forefront of Congress' attention. Texas sends more Republicans than any other state.

Cornyn added Abbott's request is "a unique situation" because the money is for "expenses that were incurred by the state that should not have been incurred by the state, but for the failure of the federal government."

House Budget Chair **Jodey Arrington** , R-Lubbock, presented a draft budget resolution Wednesday, which would include $300 billion for border security and defense spending. Arrington supports the payment to Texas, calling it "the right and responsible thing" to do. But he acknowledged he would need to make sure whatever mechanism to send out the money is fiscally responsible. That would mean collaborating with members outside of the Texas delegation.

U.S. Rep. **Chip Roy** , one of the most hawkish conservatives on reining in spending, was supportive of the reimbursement, saying Texas invested in infrastructure the federal government should have built.

"$11 billion came out of the pockets of Texans. That's money that could be used for roads, for schools, for DPS, who should have been in Austin and Dallas and Dallas and San Antonio and Houston and not down on the border," Roy said. "They were doing the job the federal government was supposed to do."

U.S. Rep. **John Carter** , R-Round Rock, serves on the House Appropriations Committee and said he was confident all Republicans on the committee would support the effort. He said it would be an easier sell because the infrastructure is already in place." TOP NEWS "Texas could sell 100 miles of border to feds, DPS has same powers as ICE, Abbott says, " Texas Tribune'sMatthew Choi -- "More than 100 miles of Texas' borderlands could be leased or sold to the federal government as part of the state's partnership with President Donald Trump to harden the border, Gov. Greg Abbott said in an interview with The Texas Tribune on Thursday. Abbott is in Washington this week to lobby Congress for $11 billion to compensate Texas for money spent on his Operation Lone Star initiative, which he said was needed to fill gaps in the Biden administration's immigration enforcement. The three-term Texas governor said he was ready to hand over to the federal government more than 50 miles of constructed border wall, nearly 20 miles of planned border walls, 100 miles of easements to build more walls, over 2,000 military beds for National Guardsmen and 4,000 jail cells to detain migrants. The exchange of real estate and working border infrastructure built under Operation Lone Star differentiates this request from past appeals Texas has made to the federal government for border enforcement, Abbott said. "This is not really a reimbursement," said Abbott during a 10-minute interview at his Washington hotel. "This is a payment for real estate assets and improvements provided by the state of Texas as payment for services rendered by the state of Texas that benefits everybody in the United States of America." Texas contains more of the southern border than any other state, stretching over 1,200 miles. Texas officials have long boasted having very little federally controlled land relative to its size. Abbott met with Texas Republicans and House Speaker Mike Johnson this week to make his case, as well as White House officials. Abbott also met with Trump last week. It remains to be seen if Congress will allocate the funds or if Trump will support the move. Slashing federal spending is among Republicans' highest priorities this year. Abbott didn't say if his meetings with Johnson or Trump yielded support, but he described them as "very appreciative of everything that Texas did, and they thank us for Texas holding the line during the four years of open border policies under [President] Joe Biden." Texas Republicans expressed unity and optimism about getting the reimbursement passed. Sen. John Cornyn has been one of the leading voices in the effort in Congress and said the Texas delegation can use its large numbers to push the priority to the forefront of Congress' attention. Texas sends more Republicans than any other state. Cornyn added Abbott's request is "a unique situation" because the money is for "expenses that were incurred by the state that should not have been incurred by the state, but for the failure of the federal government." House Budget Chair Jodey Arrington , R-Lubbock, presented a draft budget resolution Wednesday, which would include $300 billion for border security and defense spending. Arrington supports the payment to Texas, calling it "the right and responsible thing" to do. But he acknowledged he would need to make sure whatever mechanism to send out the money is fiscally responsible. That would mean collaborating with members outside of the Texas delegation. U.S. Rep. Chip Roy , one of the most hawkish conservatives on reining in spending, was supportive of the reimbursement, saying Texas invested in infrastructure the federal government should have built. "$11 billion came out of the pockets of Texans. That's money that could be used for roads, for schools, for DPS, who should have been in Austin and Dallas and Dallas and San Antonio and Houston and not down on the border," Roy said. "They were doing the job the federal government was supposed to do." U.S. Rep. John Carter , R-Round Rock, serves on the House Appropriations Committee and said he was confident all Republicans on the committee would support the effort. He said it would be an easier sell because the infrastructure is already in place." FREE SUBSCRIPTIONS HAVE ENDED : As of July 11, 2022, we have moved to a paywall for free subscribers. “**Texas could sell 100 miles of border to feds, DPS has same powers as ICE, Abbott says,** ” Texas Tribune's**Matthew Choi** — “More than 100 miles of Texas’ borderlands could be leased or sold to the federal government as part of the state’s partnership with President **Donald Trump** to harden the border, Gov. **Greg Abbott** said in an interview with The Texas Tribune on Thursday.

Abbott is in Washington this week to lobby Congress for $11 billion to compensate Texas for money spent on his Operation Lone Star initiative, which he said was needed to fill gaps in the Biden administration’s immigration enforcement. The three-term Texas governor said he was ready to hand over to the federal government more than 50 miles of constructed border wall, nearly 20 miles of planned border walls, 100 miles of easements to build more walls, over 2,000 military beds for National Guardsmen and 4,000 jail cells to detain migrants.

The exchange of real estate and working border infrastructure built under Operation Lone Star differentiates this request from past appeals Texas has made to the federal government for border enforcement, Abbott said.

“This is not really a reimbursement,” said Abbott during a 10-minute interview at his Washington hotel. “This is a payment for real estate assets and improvements provided by the state of Texas as payment for services rendered by the state of Texas that benefits everybody in the United States of America.”

Greg Abbott said in an interview with The Texas Tribune on Thursday. Abbott is in Washington this week to lobby Congress for $11 billion to compensate Texas for money spent on his Operation Lone Star initiative, which he said was needed to fill gaps in the Biden administration’s immigration enforcement. The three-term Texas governor said he was ready to hand over to the federal government more than 50 miles of constructed border wall, nearly 20 miles of planned border walls, 100 miles of easements to build more walls, over 2,000 military beds for National Guardsmen and 4,000 jail cells to detain migrants. The exchange of real estate and working border infrastructure built under Operation Lone Star differentiates this request from past appeals Texas has made to the federal government for border enforcement, Abbott said. “This is not really a reimbursement,” said Abbott during a 10-minute interview at his Washington hotel. “This is a payment for real estate assets and improvements provided by the state of Texas as payment for services rendered by the state of Texas that benefits everybody in the United States of America.” » Texas contains more of the southern border than any other state, stretching over 1,200 miles. Texas officials have long boasted having very little federally controlled land relative to its size. Abbott met with Texas Republicans and House Speaker Mike Johnson this week to make his case, as well as White House officials. Abbott also met with Trump last week. It remains to be seen if Congress will allocate the funds or if Trump will support the move. Slashing federal spending is among Republicans’ highest priorities this year. Abbott didn’t say if his meetings with Johnson or Trump yielded support, but he described them as “very appreciative of everything that Texas did, and they thank us for Texas holding the line during the four years of open border policies under [President] Joe Biden.” » Texas Republicans expressed unity and optimism about getting the reimbursement passed. Sen. John Cornyn has been one of the leading voices in the effort in Congress and said the Texas delegation can use its large numbers to push the priority to the forefront of Congress’ attention. Texas sends more Republicans than any other state. Cornyn added Abbott’s request is “a unique situation” because the money is for “expenses that were incurred by the state that should not have been incurred by the state, but for the failure of the federal government.” House Budget Chair Jodey Arrington , R-Lubbock, presented a draft budget resolution Wednesday, which would include $300 billion for border security and defense spending. Arrington supports the payment to Texas, calling it “the right and responsible thing” to do. But he acknowledged he would need to make sure whatever mechanism to send out the money is fiscally responsible. That would mean collaborating with members outside of the Texas delegation. U.S. Rep. Chip Roy , one of the most hawkish conservatives on reining in spending, was supportive of the reimbursement, saying Texas invested in infrastructure the federal government should have built. “$11 billion came out of the pockets of Texans. That's money that could be used for roads, for schools, for DPS, who should have been in Austin and Dallas and Dallas and San Antonio and Houston and not down on the border,” Roy said. “They were doing the job the federal government was supposed to do.” U.S. Rep. John Carter , R-Round Rock, serves on the House Appropriations Committee and said he was confident all Republicans on the committee would support the effort. Hi. I bet that's not what you were expecting on a big red hat these days

_(But don 't you worry, I'm about as pro-Trump as they come!)_

_My name 's Marlin Stutzman._ I'm a 4th-generation farmer raising the finest Wagyu cows this side of the Mississippi. When I'm not herding cattle and hauling hay, I'm fighting the good fight in the People's House.

I ran for office because the Democrats AND even some Republicans have stabbed farmers like me in the back for as long as I can remember.

Ask any farmer - they'll show you the scars.

**I swear elites in DC think meat and produce *magically appear* at Whole Foods - not because farmers devote their blood, sweat, and tears to their trade. **

That's how they can sleep at night knowing...
* China is buying up our farmland
* Democrats taxed us into oblivion
* Liberals want to replace beef with fake meat made from God knows what
* Politicians get rich at our expense
* We're left to pick up the scraps

My entire life is focused on bringing all that to a screeching halt. And the political class knows I can't be bought off or bribed. That's why they're mobilizing the powers-at-be to silence me so they can keep the gravy train rolling.

_And holding the line here will be tougher than a $3 steak._

**[That's why I'm left with no choice but to ask you for a small donation today to keep me in Congress. In the months ahead, Ruben's going to fight to protect Medicare and Medicaid and combat Trump, RFK Jr, Elon Musk, and anybody else in this administration as they go to war with public health.
#

Peter: Robert F. Kennedy Jr. is a maniac. Full stop.
RFK Jr is one of the people most responsible for the anti-vax movement that’s endangering our kids and all the progress we’ve made against infectious diseases.
He’s spread dangerous conspiracy theories that have no basis in reality, and demonstrated virtually no functional understanding of Medicaid and Medicare (essential parts of his job!) in his confirmation hearing.
He’s gone from being firmly pro-choice to completely backing the Trump administration’s war on abortion.
For all those reasons and more, Ruben voted against his nomination.
But after all that, he’s been confirmed as our next Secretary of Health and Human Services. It’s a serious problem — but this fight doesn’t end here.
In the months ahead, Ruben's going to fight to protect Medicare and Medicaid and combat Trump, RFK Jr., Elon Musk, and anybody else in this administration as they go to war with public health.
Arizona sent Ruben to the Senate fight, so that’s what he's going to do. But he can’t count on pallets of cash getting airdropped from a bunch of billionaire mega-donors to help power this work.

For the past few years, a cultural revolution has been tearing our country apart. In the grips of this politically correct mania, statues of George Washington were torn down, equity was championed over merit, and the insidious ideologies of DEI and ESG burrowed deep into our institutions and rewired management incentives. But the fever finally appears to be breaking.
Akin to a child declaring "The emperor isn't wearing any clothes!" the recent election marked a turning point: The vast majority of Americans realized they weren't alone in their desire to move beyond a constant focus on grievances. The pendulum reached its zenith and is swinging back towards normality. Victimhood culture is rapidly receding, and an equality of opportunity is rising in its place.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..ZF4cgAKQCcDgDFiZQ_gLsphzetjXHR63Hxk5mWHDqns?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=157094190)
Consider recent actions from some of America's largest companies. [Meta](https://substack.com/redirect/4cd2f6ec-a34d-47b5-852d-156bbc2c2ab2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) announced that it was eliminating its DEI team along with its DEI hiring practices. [Google](https://substack.com/redirect/0735ae43-ceb9-42c6-b4cf-4cc02a16368b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) terminated its use of hiring goals to boost workplace diversity and is reviewing its other DEI efforts. Even Bud Light seems to have come full circle with its "Big Men on Cul-de-Sac" Super Bowl ad that featured Peyton Manning, Post Malone and conservative comedian Shane Gillis.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/d339cb88-b2b0-44b4-97ab-195584bb4e7c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I welcome this change. Never one to shy away from speaking my mind, I have been on the frontlines pushing back against DEI in the classroom and in the boardroom. At Harvard I was reprimanded for using the term "melting pot", chastised by colleagues for asking new parents if their newborn was a boy or a girl, and finally "[canceled](https://substack.com/redirect/c70dcba5-5547-4c94-8b62-dfb26aab90da?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" when it was revealed that I had committed the cardinal sin of being a Republican. Diversity of skin color, it seemed, was important than diversity of thought.
As an advisor and director of for-profit companies, [I fought to keep the focus on shareholder value and pushed back against DEI initiatives that came at the expense of profit generation](https://substack.com/redirect/490d507e-be6e-4d0d-afcb-a0243d51d5b8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). That's what I did when I served on the board of Werner Enterprises, which generated a bit of publicity that you can read about [here](https://substack.com/redirect/43809452-9cfb-49ce-98d1-c03a51bf04cd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [here](https://substack.com/redirect/54ff1eac-b4b7-4545-be35-cfa3b21a435a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg); there's also a lively [discussion](https://substack.com/redirect/1a8e7820-4584-45ef-9e19-71ccc411c818?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of my thinking on an episode of "What's Bugging Me" entitled "D.E.I. and E.S.G. must D-I-E."
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..ZF4cgAKQCcDgDFiZQ_gLsphzetjXHR63Hxk5mWHDqns?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=157094190)
I've always believed, like Milton Friedman's similarly titled essay, that the **social responsibility of business is to increase its profits** , _period_. Boardrooms and C-Suites need to focus on delivering high-quality products and services to their customers at prices that enable both customers and producers to share in value creation. Doing so will enable profits that shareholders can utilize as they see fit, for social or other purposes. Management teams that prioritize social objectives, however, at the expense of profits are harming shareholders by both reducing their shareholder returns and by deploying those returns towards efforts that those shareholders may not believe are worthy.
* * *

This is not to suggest that energy efficiency or efforts to expand the workforce are harmful. In fact, in many cases, the pursuit of energy efficiency can also lower cost and increase profits - while simultaneously helping the environment. Likewise, recruiting from under-represented communities can often lead to the identification of hidden talent and a better workforce. Such efforts, if motivated by the pursuit of profits, generate social benefit. The driver, however, needs to be the bottom-line.
* * *
#### Mentions of "DEI" or "Diversity, Equity, Inclusion" during quarterly earnings calls of publicly-traded companies
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/049e1561-4ed6-4c18-9f7f-f59c125f754a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Source: [Axios](https://substack.com/redirect/7d2113cb-12c6-4ebe-8602-e590dcc59aa6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
A long-overdue return to focusing on shareholder value is gaining momentum in Corporate America. Still, a few [holdouts](https://substack.com/redirect/94dce077-56ac-4639-8592-1382de6845ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) remain. Some companies refuse, like WWII Japanese soldiers hiding out in the jungles of the Pacific, unaware that the war is over, to surrender. But for the vast majority of businesses, however, the lessons drawn from [Bud Light's ill-fated foray into politics](https://substack.com/redirect/d5a0a401-9e25-451d-a56d-7c08ec78df49?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) are clear: **The business of business is, well, business**.

The downfall of DEI is helping business return to its purpose | | | Feb 13 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- For the past few years, a cultural revolution has been tearing our country apart. In the grips of this politically correct mania, statues of George Washington were torn down, equity was championed over merit, and the insidious ideologies of DEI and ESG burrowed deep into our institutions and rewired management incentives. But the fever finally appears to be breaking. Akin to a child declaring "The emperor isn't wearing any clothes!" the recent election marked a turning point: The vast majority of Americans realized they weren't alone in their desire to move beyond a constant focus on grievances. The pendulum reached its zenith and is swinging back towards normality. Victimhood culture is rapidly receding, and an equality of opportunity is rising in its place. Consider recent actions from some of America's largest companies. announced that it was eliminating its DEI team along with its DEI hiring practices. terminated its use of hiring goals to boost workplace diversity and is reviewing its other DEI efforts. Even Bud Light seems to have come full circle with its "Big Men on Cul-de-Sac" Super Bowl ad that featured Peyton Manning, Post Malone and conservative comedian Shane Gillis. I welcome this change. Never one to shy away from speaking my mind, I have been on the frontlines pushing back against DEI in the classroom and in the boardroom. At Harvard I was reprimanded for using the term "melting pot", chastised by colleagues for asking new parents if their newborn was a boy or a girl, and finally "" when it was revealed that I had committed the cardinal sin of being a Republican. Diversity of skin color, it seemed, was important than diversity of thought. As an advisor and director of for-profit companies, . That's what I did when I served on the board of Werner Enterprises, which generated a bit of publicity that you can read about and ; there's also a lively of my thinking on an episode of "What's Bugging Me" entitled "D.E.I. and E.S.G. must D-I-E." I've always believed, like Milton Friedman's similarly titled essay, that the social responsibility of business is to increase its profits , period. Boardrooms and C-Suites need to focus on delivering high-quality products and services to their customers at prices that enable both customers and producers to share in value creation. Doing so will enable profits that shareholders can utilize as they see fit, for social or other purposes. Management teams that prioritize social objectives, however, at the expense of profits are harming shareholders by both reducing their shareholder returns and by deploying those returns towards efforts that those shareholders may not believe are worthy. | | | | ---|---|--- | February 27, 2024 | This is not to suggest that energy efficiency or efforts to expand the workforce are harmful. In fact, in many cases, the pursuit of energy efficiency can also lower cost and increase profits - while simultaneously helping the environment. Likewise, recruiting from under-represented communities can often lead to the identification of hidden talent and a better workforce. Such efforts, if motivated by the pursuit of profits, generate social benefit. The driver, however, needs to be the bottom-line. Mentions of "DEI" or "Diversity, Equity, Inclusion" during quarterly earnings calls of publicly-traded companies | | ---|---|--- Source: A long-overdue return to focusing on shareholder value is gaining momentum in Corporate America. Still, a few remain. Some companies refuse, like WWII Japanese soldiers hiding out in the jungles of the Pacific, unaware that the war is over, to surrender. But for the vast majority of businesses, however, the lessons drawn from are clear: The business of business is, well, business. | | ---|---|--- VIKRAM MANSHARAMANI is an entrepreneur, consultant, scholar, neighbor, husband, father, volunteer, and professional generalist who thinks in multiple-dimensions and looks beyond the short-term. Self-taught to think around corners and connect original dots, he spends his time speaking with global leaders in business, government, academia, and journalism. He's currently the Chairman and CEO of Goodwell Foods, a manufacturer of private label frozen pizza. LinkedIn has twice listed him as its #1 Top Voice in Money & Finance, and Worth profiled him as one of the 100 Most Powerful People in Global Finance. Vikram earned a PhD From MIT, has taught at Yale and Harvard, and is the author of three books, , and **. Vikram lives in Lincoln, New Hampshire with his wife and two children, where they can usually be found hiking or skiing. | I hear you, team –

The administration’s actions to take over Treasury payment systems are a direct threat to the privacy and security of Americans’ most sensitive personal information. Over the past few weeks, we’ve received thousands of calls from folks in the district concerned about Elon Musk and DOGE’s overreach of the Treasury and personal data.

_**That’s why I’m responding with action.**_

**Last week, I drafted and introduced my original bill–the CLEAR Act (Consistent Legal Expectations and Access to Records Act). This bill will ensure that temporary agencies like DOGE are subject to the same Freedom of Information Act rules as permanent government entities.**

Peter, Donald Trump's attempt to defund critical services is the biggest threat to the Bronx that I have witnessed in my eleven years as an elected official. subject: Donald Trump is taking away money from the American people — and handing it back to the mega-corporations ripping off consumers.

body:
[ https://act.adamschiff.com/go/62?t=1001&akid=8305%2E5257348%2EMVmJBj ]Adam Schiff for Senate

Donald Trump and Elon Musk are pulling off an opposite Robin Hood scheme —
taking money from working people and handing it back to the ultra-wealthy.

Here’s what’s going on,
Derek.

The primary agency responsible for protecting Americans from large
corporations victimizing consumers — the Consumer Financial Protection
Bureau (CFPB) — has just been shuttered by Trump and Elon Musk. This
agency has saved Americans $21 billion by holding corporations
accountable. Just last month, it sued Capitol One for failing to pay
customers over $2 billion they were owed.

After the 2008 financial crisis, a bipartisan group of senators voted to
create the CFPB to enforce transparency and prevent illegal activity from
banks and financial lenders.

So, of course, Trump is dismantling it — to protect his billionaire donors
and mega-corporate allies, including Elon Musk, who stands to benefit
directly.

Musk is aggressively expanding his financial services empire through X by
rolling out digital payment options — and the CFPB is one of the key
agencies overseeing digital payment platforms. Just last year, the CFPB
proposed a rule to regulate large digital wallets and payment apps —
something that would have impacted Musk’s financial ambitions. By
eliminating the CFPB, Musk would be able to operate his financial ventures
unchecked, avoiding consumer protections and compliance costs while
profiting at the expense of working Americans.

Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) has also taken control
of key systems within the CFPB, effectively stalling oversight of big tech
companies and halting critical investigations. This isn’t about policy —
it’s about billionaires rigging the system to enrich themselves.

By gutting the CFPB, Trump is giving corporate America a green light to
steal from consumers, while working families foot the bill. It’s an
intentional redistribution of wealth — away from everyday Americans and
into the pockets of the ultra-rich.

We can’t let them get away with this,
Derek.

I’m joining my fellow Senate Democrats to expose Trump and Musk’s reckless
dismantling of consumer protections. Trump’s so-called “MAGA promise” is a
farce — his policies serve only himself and his wealthiest allies, while
everyday Americans pay the price.
